Subject: Re: Eval capacity — short follow-up on burst and runway

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. We ran a short load test this morning and hit a couple of limits on concurrent requests during our batch ingest simulation.

Two asks from our end before we sign off on conversion:
- Can we get a short runway extension (2 extra weeks) to validate a throttled production path?
- During that runway, we would like a small pool of burst capacity (on-demand) to handle spikes — ideally billed as credits rather than a permanent SKU increase.

We are under a compressed procurement timeline; legal would prefer a single, concise amendment rather than a full SOW. Attaching the log excerpts separately. Can you propose a simple packaging option (timebox + burst credits) and a one-time concession to cover the extension?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Sarah

Sarah Lin

(sarah@clearbay.ai)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 17:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Eval capacity — scaled trial proposal attached

Hi Sarah — thanks for the context and the excerpts. Attached is a short proposal with two options that map to what you described. TL;DR summary: both options keep the existing timebox but add a 14-day runway plus a small burst credit pool; the difference is how credits are priced and whether ClearBay takes a temporary SKU tier bump.

Option A — Timebox + Burst Credits (recommended)
- +14 days to current evaluation window (no change to per-token rates).
- 50k burst credits preloaded (usable for peak traffic), expires at end of runway.
- One-time concession: 10% credit against the first invoice if ClearBay converts to a Reserved Tier within 30 days of conversion.

Option B — Temporary Tier Upgrade
- +14 days to window.
- Move to a temporary higher concurrency SKU for the runway (same unit rates as higher SKU).
- Redwood covers 50% of the incremental SKU cost for the runway as a one-time credit.

Notes/Constraints
- Burst credits are single-use tokens that apply only to bursts over the baseline capacity and cannot be carried beyond the runway.
- Any sustained usage beyond baseline after the runway will be billed at normal overage rates unless a reserved commit is signed.
- We can do a short amendment to your MSA — attached a two-page amendment and a simple summary of terms.

I copied Marissa and Ben for approval on the concession language. If that looks reasonable to you I can push a DocuSign link for the amendment and request a countersign from contracts.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
